title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
statement: You get the first node of a singly linked list and a number n. Remove the n-th node counting from the end (n = 1 is the last node). Return the first node of the list afterwards. Try to do it in a single walk.

example.caption: n = 2 means the second node from the end. That is 4, so it is removed.

idea.sentence: Keep two pointers exactly n nodes apart and slide them together. When the front one is on the last node, the back one stands right before the node to remove.

jargon.plain: A throwaway node placed before the head. It means every node, even the head, has a node before it that you can relink.
The distance between slow and fast, counted in nodes. It stays fixed while both move.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the node values, then n, e.g. [1,2,3,4,5], 2

compare.bruteLabel: Pass 1 counts the length. Pass 2 walks to the node

rows.name: Count, then walk
rows.note: Two passes: first the length L, then L - n steps to the node before the target.

rows.name: Two pointers with a gap
rows.note: One pass. The gap replaces the counting.

fast.takeaway: Both are linear and use no extra memory. The gap trick saves the first counting pass and is the pattern to remember.

stages.title: Dummy and two pointers
stages.note: Add a fake node before the head. slow and fast both start on it.

stages.title: Open the gap
stages.note: Move fast n nodes ahead. Now slow and fast are n apart.

stages.title: Slide together
stages.note: Move both one step at a time until fast is on the last node. The gap stays n.

stages.title: Unlink
stages.note: slow is just before the target. Set slow.next to the node after the target.

stages.title: Return dummy.next
stages.note: This is the real head. It changes when the head itself was removed.

edges.title: Only node
edges.why: slow stays on the dummy. Unlinking makes dummy.next null, so the answer is empty.

edges.title: Remove the head
edges.why: The target is the first node, so slow must stand before it. Only the dummy is before it.

edges.title: Remove the tail
edges.why: fast moves one step, then the loop is skipped. slow is on 1 and cuts off 2.

edges.title: n equals the length
edges.why: Same as removing the head. fast lands on the last node right after the gap is made.

gotchas.text: Start both pointers on the dummy, not on the head. Then slow ends one node before the target, which is where you need it to relink.
Return dummy.next, not head. When the head is the node you removed, the old head is gone.
fast.next has the type ListNode | null. Inside the gap loop you need fast.next! (safe when 1 <= n <= length). Without the promise from the problem, check for null instead.
If n is larger than the list, fast becomes nil and fast.Next panics with a nil pointer error. The problem guarantees n is valid, but real code should check.

recap.pattern: Linked list: gap between two pointers
recap.key: Start both on a dummy. Move fast n steps. Move both until fast.next is null. Then slow.next is the node to remove.
